conviction_note: The print will be judged on the Q4 guide. A direct peer (Enphase, 27 Oct) guided Q4 sell-through down about 10% with Europe sell-through already down 12% q/q, and the one dated sell-side Q4 number (Northland $300M) sits well below the single, undated aggregator consensus ($343.4M). Against that, the Q3 print will probably land at or above the $325M guide midpoint, plus $11.5M of IEEPA refunds the guide excluded, and the short is crowded (18.2% of shares out, 4.5 days to cover, 25d skew +23.9 already paying for downside). The findings net to about +0.2 and the scaled number is a slight negative lean (p_up 47 on a 14% abs move). The gap between them is the guide risk sitting in p_up rather than in any single sourced number.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue: company guide $310-340M (midpoint $325M), non-GAAP GM 22-26% ex IEEPA refunds, non-GAAP opex $86-91M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001419612/000117891326003833/exhibit_99-1.htm, 2026-08-05). Aggregator consensus $330.5M revenue / -$0.02 non-GAAP EPS (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SEDG/earnings-forecasts, undated). Zacks/EarningsWhispers $377M and Chartmill $375.3M are pre-guide and stale. The Q4 2026 bar is DISPUTED: Benzinga $343.4M (single source, undated) against Northland's $300M (https://www.finanztrends.de/news/solaredge-aktie-northland-senkt-umsatzschaetzungen/, 2026-10-02). Guidance-line findings are capped small for that reason.
positioning_check: Short interest 11,199,638 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 18.20% of shares outstanding (61.5M per the 10-Q cover), 4.46 days to cover, down 1.5% from 11.38M on 09-30 (https://altindex.com/ticker/sedg/short-interest; corroborated for 09-30 by https://massive.com/quote/sedg). Baseline: 25d skew +23.9 vol points (downside paid), ATM IV 162%, event-implied move 12.84%, put/call OI 0.65, spot $32.12, -59% from 52w high, 20d run-up -5.6%. The stock fell about 10% to ~$29 on 2026-10-29 on Enphase's guide and has since recovered to $32.12. Crowded short, and puts are already bid.

findings.finding: Enphase's Q3 2026 release (27 Oct, after SolarEdge last spoke) shows European sell-through down 12% q/q, worst in France, and Europe revenue down about 11%. US sell-through fell 35% y/y. Enphase guided Q4 revenue to $225-255M (midpoint about 18% below Q3's $293.3M) on an assumed further 10% fall in sell-through. That is negative read-through for a SolarEdge Q4 guide that leans on Europe, where SolarEdge's revenue more than doubled y/y in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SEDG falls hard on weak guides: on 2026-08-05 it fell 30.5% when the Q3 guide of $310-340M came in below the then ~$375M consensus, despite a Q2 beat. It fell 10% to $29 on 2026-10-29 on this Enphase release (https://now.solar/2026/10/29/enphase-energy-sinks-20-on-weak-q4-guidance-as-residential-solar-slump-deepens-solaredge-drops-10-sunrun-falls-5-first-solar-dips-24-7-wall-st/) and then recovered to $32.12.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: SEDG lost 10% on the day, then recovered all of it. A fully priced read-through would have left the stock at or below $29; it sits at $32.12. Two things limit the transmission. SolarEdge's Q3 guide already embedded about $15M of European seasonal decline, and SolarEdge is more exposed to Europe storage/three-phase (Nexis) and US C&I than to the micro-inverter resi channel Enphase serves.
findings.independence: Peer proxy, not a SolarEdge number. Tigo cut its FY2026 outlook in August on weak US, Italian and Czech resi (https://investors.tigoenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/tigo-energy-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). Different source, same direction on resi.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-02 Northland cut its SolarEdge Q4 2026 revenue estimate from $340M to $300M, and FY2026 from $1.33B to $1.29B; FY2027 to $1.34B, about $110M below consensus, citing management's cautious year-end remarks. The only aggregator Q4 consensus found is $343.4M (Benzinga, undated), so a Q4 guide midpoint near $300-320M would miss the posted consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide below consensus: -30.5% on 2026-08-05 (Q3 guide midpoint $325M against about $375M consensus). Q1 2026 (2026-05-06, Q2 guide $325-355M): -9.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: A published sell-side note, so the buy-side has seen it. What may be unpriced is that aggregator Q4 consensus still reads $343.4M. If the street had fully absorbed a ~$300M Q4, that figure would have fallen toward $310-320M. The Q4 bar itself is single-sourced and disputed, so this finding is capped small.
findings.independence: The Enphase Q4 guide (finding 1) points the same way from a different source. SolarEdge's 2026-10-01 CRO resignation 8-K (finding 5) is a separate weak signal.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue will probably land at or above the $325M guide midpoint. SolarEdge printed Q2 at $346.2M against a $325-355M guide (midpoint $340M) and Q4 2025 at $335.4M against $310-340M (midpoint $325M). The Q3 guide also excludes the $11.5M of IEEPA refunds received in July, which the company says flips the midpoint to a non-GAAP operating profit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats inside a known guide are sold or ignored when the next guide disappoints: the Q2 beat (revenue above midpoint, first non-GAAP operating profit in three years, EPS +7c) went with -30.5%. The Q3 2025 beat with strong numbers went with +28.9% (2025-11-05).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It lands inside what the company guided, and the July refund was disclosed in the release. The only unpriced part is how far above the $330.5M aggregator consensus the print comes, which is sized small. The refund is a one-off below the operating line in substance, so it is worth a fraction of the same dollars as operating profit.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 release (Q2 guide $325-355M, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001419612/000117891326002404/exhibit_99-1.htm) is the other document the beat pattern rests on. The same company is the issuer, so this is not independent of SolarEdge.

findings.finding: Crowded short into the print: 11.2M shares short, 18.2% of shares outstanding, 4.46 days to cover (15 Oct settlement). The 25d skew is already +23.9 vol points toward puts, and the stock is 59% off its 52-week high, so a Q4 guide that merely avoids a disaster has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two of the last seven prints moved more than +15% (2025-02-19 +16.0%, 2025-11-05 +28.9%). Both came with short interest well above 15% of float.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the market's own bet, so this is not information the market lacks. It is the asymmetry: the downside the skew pays for is held by shorts who must buy on any relief. If the squeeze were priced, call IV would be bid relative to puts; the skew shows the opposite.
findings.independence: https://massive.com/quote/sedg gives 11.38M short and 4.6 days at 09-30, a separate tracker with the same FINRA basis.

findings.finding: SolarEdge's Chief Revenue Officer Daniel Huber resigned on 1 October 2026, effective 31 March 2027, with his 2026 bonus paid and 'not the result of any disagreement' (8-K Item 5.02). The commercial head is leaving one month before the Q3 print and the Q4 guide; no replacement was named in the filing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline reaction to an officer change. The 8-K brought no visible price move in the October tape (the stock's large October move was the 29 Oct Enphase day).
findings.why_not_priced: Little-noticed filing that made no headline beyond feeds. If it were read as a signal of weak bookings, it would have appeared in previews or in the October tape. It is weak evidence: the bonus is paid and the six-month notice suggests an orderly exit.

findings.finding: On 28 July 2026 the FCC added foreign-produced power inverters to the Covered List, blocking new authorizations; 45X-eligible US-made inverters are exempt. UBS (31 Aug) said the ban could affect about 50% of the US market and upgraded SolarEdge to Buy with a $42 target on share gains, since most of its inverters and optimizers are now made in the US. The Q3 call is the first full quarter in which management can quantify share or bookings from this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The UBS upgrade drove a rally in early September (https://www.tikr.com/blog/solaredge-stock-ubs-upgrade-buy-fcc-inverter-policy); the stock has since given it back.
findings.why_not_priced: The policy is public. What is not yet priced is any company-quantified share gain in US resi or C&I. If the market credited it, the stock would not trade 59% off its high with puts bid. It is a sign against a strong skew, so it is sized small: the option market is pricing the US resi slump, and this offsets only part of that.
findings.independence: FCC scope described by law firms (https://www.stoel.com/insights/publications/it-happened-fcc-adds-foreign-produced-power-inverters-to-the-covered-list), a different source on the same policy.

findings.finding: At the 10 September 2026 Investor Day SolarEdge cited $1.7B of firm contracts for delivery through 2030 (safe-harbor and enterprise), US C&I rooftop share up from 29% (Q4 2024) to 57% (Q2 2026), and a 29% US share. That gives the Q4/2027 outlook a contracted floor that a resi-led Enphase read-through does not capture.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not a print line. Jefferies after Investor Day kept Hold at $31 and called SEDG 'an unappealing short, not a compelling long' (https://stock3.com/news/solaredge-jefferies-sieht-den-turnaround-geschafft-aber-haelt-die-charttechnische-basis-17282356).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since it was disclosed in September. It matters only if the Q4 guide shows the contracts converting, which the market discounts after the Northland cut. This is a third-party summary of the event, not the slides, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Shares the company as source with finding 6 (US share); not independent of it.

outside_window.finding: The Netherlands' net metering (salderingsregeling) ends on 1 January 2027 (per Enphase's Q3 release). That shifts Dutch resi demand toward storage retrofits in 2027, a market where SolarEdge is strong. The effect shows in 2027 bookings, not in this print's window, beyond whatever the Q4 guide says.

baseline_tension: The negative guide read-through agrees with the +23.9 put skew and the 20d run-up of -5.6%, so it is largely priced. The crowded short (18.2%) and the full recovery from the 10-29 Enphase drop cut against more downside, which keeps p_up near 50 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives; at 18.2% of shares out): Enphase read-through -1.0 to -0.7, CRO resignation -0.3 to -0.2.

Lesson 6 (bar single-sourced or disputed): the Q4 consensus is $343.4M from one undated aggregator against Northland's $300M, so the Northland guide finding was capped from -1.0 to -0.6 and p_up moved toward 50 (46 to 47).

Lessons 2 and 6 (inside the guide; refund is a one-off): Q3 beat-vs-midpoint finding +0.8 to +0.4, because it lands inside what the company guided and the $11.5M refund is disclosed below-the-line money.

Lesson 7 (a sign against a strong skew needs a reason or a smaller size): FCC share-gain finding +0.5 to +0.3, Investor Day contracts +0.3 to +0.2; the positioning finding was trimmed +1.0 to +0.8 but kept, because the squeeze is the stated reason the skew may be wrong.
Lesson 1: print_vs_bar trimmed from +2.0 to +1.5 and kept small in the reaction, because this name sold a Q2 beat by 30% on the guide.
abs_move_pct left at 14 (implied 12.84, median 11.22; a new-period guide and a crowded short both argue against shrinking it).
